chapter: Probation, Las Vegas and Los Angeles in the 1950s
title: Benny Carter let go, Sweets' combo and the hotel closing overnight
summary: The hotel replaced Carter's band, then trucked out the casino money and closed.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah. And so when I got there for the second Benny Carter band, he was out of jail. So the hotel served a very short notice on Benny Carter and told him that they were going to pay him two weeks' money in order for Les Brown to come in, the main dining room. So Benny didn't give them any lip or anything. He packed up, bag and baggage, and told the band that that was their last night. And they gave him half of the money and told him to come back the next week and they'd give him the other half, you know, for the two weeks' pay. Well, now, Sweets said, 'Well, man, let's stay here. They want me to take a combo into the Casino, and when Benny comes back we'll get that money and we'll still be working here.' You know.

Yeah. I said, 'All right.' So I'm around in the annex part. I've got me a room around there, you know. I'm not living in the main hotel. Someone came around and said, 'Man, you still in bed.' I said, 'What else am I supposed to be doing?' He said, 'Man, they've got trucks backed

up, they're taking all the money out of the casino, they're closing the hotel." I jumped up and said, "What?" And I'm looking forward to payday the next day, and they're taking all this money out of the hotel. The hotel's closed. Now what do we do? They had combos from all over the United States, some from Canada, playing in the casino, you know, alternating.

Well, they had King Kolax there. They had the Platters. That was the Platters' first job. And some group out of Canada. I can't remember the name of it. And they had an organist whose name was Jackie. Jackie Davis I think was his name. He was playing then like Jimmy Smith, you know.
I don't know. Probably died. Because he was a very good organist. I don't see any other reason to stop him from playing or being known other than death.
How long all together was the Moulin Rouge open? Do you know?
Oh, it wasn't open hardly a year.
A year at the maximum, and I don't think it was a year.
It doesn't seem like it was that long.
No, because it just had time for two bands in there, you know, so it was opened and closed.
